5. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.01.2023.
1) Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.11.2021 due

In his examination in chief, he stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident. He denied any rash or negligent act on his part in driving of the offending vehicle. He stated that the petitioner/victims have falsely implicated him and that FIR no. 206/21 has been lodged with a motive to extort money from the respondents. He stated that none of the alleged victims were travelling in the offending vehicle. He relied upon his identity card as Ex.R1W1/1. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. Page no. 5 of 25(ss) It has been argued on behalf of the petitioner that since petitioner has suffered injury on account of accident that is proved to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, respondent no.3, with which the offending vehicle was insured, may be directed to compensate the petitioner. 
On the other hand, it is argued by respondent no.1 and 2 that the petitioner has failed to prove rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 or the involvement of the vehicle in the alleged accident. It is further argued that even if the accident is assumed to be proved, it is respondent no.3 which is liable to compensate the petitioner. It is argued on behalf of respondent no.3 that the petitioner/victims were traveling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized and gratuitous passengers since the offending vehicle was a goods carriage vehicle. It is argued that the offending vehicle was insured as a goods carriage vehicle and could not carry any passenger except for the driver and owner of the goods. It is further argued that the insured i.e.
respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims. 
10. Now, on the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under :

Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1AE-4509 (Eicher Canter) being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? OPP.
11. Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs.
Ravindra Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21 Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83070665/
4 Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 
12. In the present case, the injured /petitioner has specifically deposed about accident dated 07.11.2021. He has categorically stated that at the time of the accident, offending vehicle bearing no.
DL-1LAE-4509 was being driven by Respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner. He has deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle deliberately ignored the warnings to be slow and careful. It is due to his rash and negligent driving that the offending vehicle overturned with the sudden and forceful impact causing injuries to its passengers and death of one of them. 
13. In the present case, the Tribunal takes judicial notice of the CHARU GUPTA Date:

0rs. Page no. 7 of 25(ss) fact that a common evidence has been recorded by one single Local Commissioner in all the 13 connected matters. It is a matter of record that injured victims namely Vishal Majumdar, Debu Das, Deepak Das and Ganesh Das have also been examined as eye witnesses /victims in all the cases. Apart from the testimony of the petitioner, testimony of other victims regarding the factum of accident, manner of accident, rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, is coherent and suffers from no apparent discrepancy. All the victims have corroborated that despite being repeatedly cautioned, driver of the offending vehicle continued to drive at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and lost control/balance while taking a sharp turn. 
Though the respondents have denied that the offending vehicle was hired by Ganesh Das or anyone else for the purpose of idol immersion, reporting of the matter immediately to the police on the same date sizure of the vehicle by the police on the same date, preparation of MLCs of the victims as well as respondent no.1 at the same time and in the same hospital as well as filing of chargesheet by the investigating officer after thorough investigation of the accident, supports the plea of the petitioners. It has been held in National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi that the completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 
It is further observed that though respondent no.1 and 2 denied occurrence of the accident in their evidence as R1W1 and R2W1 respectively, during cross examination of R1W1 (i.e. respondent no.1/driver), such witness admitted being driver of CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 MACT No. 332/22 GUPTA Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 8 of 25(ss) 04:17:38 +0530 the offending vehicle on the date of accident. Though he volunteered to state that he was not driving the said vehicle at the time of the alleged accident, he admitted that at around 02:00 p.m he took the vehicle from Lodhi Road Bus Stand and was going towards Chhatarpur. On further cross-examination he stated that he was not injured in the Ravindra Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21 Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83070665/
5 said accident, but on the contrary, also admitted that his medical record of treatment was prepared at AIIMS Hospital on the date of accident. The admission on the part of respondent no.1 regarding being driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time and the fact that he was taken to AIIMS Hospital for treatment on the date of accident, proves the factum of occurrence of the accident. Since no evidence has been led by the respondents to show that respondent no.1 was not driving the offending vehicle rashly or negligently, by preponderance of probabilities, claim of the victims that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1,
stands proved. 
It has also been pleaded on behalf of the insurance company that since the victim was under the influence of alcohol and was out on the streets in violation of the Covid-19 Pandemic guidelines, deduction in respect of contributory negligence also be made. 
There is nothing in the MLC of the petitioner to show that he was intoxicated. In the considered opinion of this Tribunal, intoxication by the victim (mere passenger in a vehicle) or breach of pandemic protocol issued only for safety from the pandemic, are not grounds that contributed to the occurrence to the accident and hence no deduction qua contributory negligence is permissible. CHARU by GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 04:17:43 +0530 MACT No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra &
0rs. Page no. 9 of 25(ss) 
14 . In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioners have been able to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question, took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 by its driver/respondent no.1 on the date and time of accident. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners/claimants and against the respondents. 
Issue no. 2 Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 
15. As regards the issue of liability of the respondents, respondent no.3 has raised a statutory defence pleading that the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy in as much as the offending vehicle held RC as a goods carriage vehicle and was not permitted to carry victims as passengers. It is further pleaded that since the son of the petitioner no.1 and all other injured victims were mere gratuitous passengers travelling in the offending vehicle without authorization, insurance company is not liable to compensate them. 
In order to establish this defence, respondent no.3 has examined Sh. Parth Arya, Deputy Manger (legal claims) as R3W1. R3W1 has duly proved the terms and conditions of the insurance policy which clearly do not cover the use of offending vehicle as a passenger vehicle. Since it stands proved in issue no.1 that the offending vehicle was carrying the victims as gratuitous passengers, there is certainly a breach of the terms and Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2024.10.21 04:17:51 +0530 MACT No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 10 of 25(ss) conditions of insurance policy.

6 Now, whether the payment of compensation is to made jointly by the owner and driver of the vehicle or by the insurer which could thereafter be recovered by the owner and driver, has to be considered in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anu Bhanvara vs. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company AIR 2019 SC 3934. In the said judgment, Apex Court held that the insurance of the vehicle, though as a goods vehicle, is not disputed by the parties. It held that since the claimants were young children who suffered permanent disability on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the principle of "pay and recover" should be directed to be invoked in the present case. The court accordingly held that the insurance company shall have right to realize the compensation amount from the driver and owner of the vehicle in accordance with the law. 
Reliance is also placed on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manuara Khatoon vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh AIR 2017 SC 1204, wherein the court while referring to the case of Manager, National Insurance company Ltd. vs. Saju P. Paul & anr. (2013) 2SCC observed :
"...16. This question also fell for consideration recently in Manager, National Insurance Company Limited vs. Saju P. Paul & Anr., (supra) wherein this Court took note of entire previous case law on the subject mentioned above and examined the question in the context of Section 147 of the Act. While allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company by reversing the judgment of the High Court, it was held on facts that since the victim was travelling in offending vehicle as "gratuitous passenger" and hence, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to suffer the liability arising out of accident on the Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date:
MACT No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 11 of 25(ss) 04:17:56 +0530 strength of the insurance policy. However, this Court keeping in view the benevolent object of the Act and other relevant factors arising in the case, issued the directions against the Insurance Company to pay the awarded sum to the claimants and then to recover the said sum from the insured in the same proceedings by applying the principle of "pay and recover". 
17. Justice R.M. Lodha (as His Lordship then was and later became CJI) speaking for the Bench held in paras 20 and 26 as under:
"20. The next question that arises for consideration is whether in the peculiar facts of this case a direction could be issued to the Insurance Company to first satisfy the awarded amount in favour of the claimant and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle (Respondent 2 herein).
26. The pendency of consideration of the above questions by a larger Bench does not mean that the course that was followed in Baljit Kaur, (2004) 2 SCC 1 and Challa Upendra Rao, (2004) 8 SCC 517 should not be followed, more so in a peculiar fact situation of this case. In the present case, the accident occurred in 1993. At that time,
the claimant was 28 years old. He is now about 48 years. The claimant was a driver Ravindra Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21 Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83070665/

He has not been able to get compensation so far due to the stay order passed by this Court. 
He cannot be compelled to struggle further for recovery of the amount. The Insurance Company has already deposited the entire awarded amount pursuant to the order of this Court passed on 1-8-2011 (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Saju P. Paul, SLP No. 20127 of 2011 and the said amount has been invested in a fixed deposit account. Having regard to these peculiar facts of the case in hand,
we are satisfied that the claimant (Respondent 1) may be allowed to withdraw the amount deposited by the Insurance Company before this Court along with accrued interest. The Insurance Company (the appellant) thereafter may recover the amount so paid from the owner (Respondent 2 herein).

In view of the foregoing discussion, we are of the view that the direction to United India Insurance Company (respondent No. 3) - they being the insurer of the offending vehicle which was found involved in causing accident due to negligence of its driver needs to be issued directing them (United India Insurance Company-respondent No.3) to first pay the awarded sum to the appellants (claimants) and then to recover the paid awarded sum from the owner of the offending vehicle (Tata Sumo)-respondent No.1 in execution proceedings arising in this very case as per the law laid down in Para 26 of Saju P. Paul's case quoted supra..." 
As such, as respondent no. 3 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner however, entitled to recovery rights from driver and owner of the offending vehicle. 
16. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:18:05 Date:
2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 13 of 25(ss) physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 
17. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses. 
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

17.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a)

future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
17.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence.

18. As per record Adhar Card of petitioner (neither exhibited nor denied by the respondents), show his year of birth as 1988 Accordingly, at the time of accident, his age would been approximately 33 years. 
19. As per MLC (neither exhibited nor denied by the respondents) and discharge summary,
victim/injured suffered RTI with blunt trauma chest with left multiple rib fracture with occult pneumothorax. He was admitted on 07.11.2021 and discharged on 12.11.2021 i.e. 6 days. No proof of educational qualification or employment has been filed. As such, keeping in view the age of the victim /injured, he is assumed to have been working atleast as an unskilled labour. His income has to be thus assessed that of an unskilled labour, prevailing in Delhi at the time of accident i.e.
Rs.618/- per day. Having regard to the nature of injury suffered by him, it is assumed that the injured would have been incapacitated from working or earning for atleast one month. He would have thus suffered a loss of income of Rs.618X30=18540/-.
20. No medical bills have been placed on record and as such no compensation can be granted under this head. 
No compensation towards future loss of income can be granted in cases where petitioner has not proved to have sustained any permanent disability.
